text:
Back on Nov. 11, Tampa Bay put eight goals on Buffalo. On Sunday, on the second night of a back-to-back and a day after a 4-3 loss in Florida, the Sabres returned the favor with a 6-2 win at Benchmark International Arena that ended their road trip on a high.

It did not start like a rout. Tampa Bay owned the first period, 1.42 expected goals to 0.68 (the quality of chances), and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen had to stop Brayden Point on a good look to keep it level. Jiri Kulich had scored early for Buffalo on a 5% chance, and Nikita Kucherov tied it on the power play at 12:21, set up by Jake Guentzel and John Carlson. Kucherov, who asked the Lightning for a trade earlier this month, remains the centre of the story in Tampa.

The second period swung it. Jack Quinn scored 1:22 in, the goal that moved Buffalo from 48% to 66% to win. Tage Thompson then scored twice, a slap shot on the power play at 11:05 and a snap shot at 16:17, both set up by Zach Benson. Gage Goncalves pulled one back early in the third, but Noah Ostlund answered a minute later off a pass from Peyton Krebs, and Benson finished it with an empty-netter. Benson had a goal and two assists and the best individual chance of the night, a 63% look that Dennis Hildeby stopped.

The final score oversells the gap. Tampa Bay had 69 shot attempts to 42, the teams were nearly even on expected goals (3.41 Buffalo, 3.34 Tampa Bay), and our replays of every shot made it close to a coin flip, 51% Sabres. The difference was in net. Luukkonen made 29 saves, 1.34 better than expected, and led everyone in wins added; Joe Yerdon of Bleacher Report noted it was his 100th career win. Hildeby allowed 1.6 goals more than his 27 shots deserved.

For Buffalo, the top line of Kulich, Thompson and Benson did most of the damage: Thompson's two goals, Kulich's opener and Benson's empty-netter, which Kulich set up. That is a line worth watching when the Sabres get back on the road after Thanksgiving.
headline: Thompson scores twice as Sabres flip the Lightning script
